title: Check the caller contract and owner lifetime before repairing a helper
applies_when: An isolated reproduction alleges a missing method decorator, script global, cache-key collision, stale object identity, constant self-comparison, returned-field loss or exception-path resource leak, but omits the full helper implementation, ordered result assembly, interface or owner that invokes it.
lesson: Read the declared interface, actual invocation and owner lifetime before choosing a regression. A receiver named cls is not a classmethod without its descriptor. Follow id-cache creation, strong references, replacement and invalidation together. Check __main__ global initialization and platform-validity predicates before inventing import-only or constant-self-comparison failures. Outer request/stream handlers may shield cleanup after a throwing helper. Fetch the relevant reset/reuse tests, not just their first window. Inspect every earlier spread and later overwrite before alleging returned-field loss: skipping a conditional spread does not remove ...result's fields. Test empty/nonempty contributions and the supported entry with a normal control. Acquire missing context before installing dependencies; do not remove references the real owner retains. An absent newly invented method proves a feature delta, not a regression. Read feature-request alternatives: static profile matching is not capacity, runtime or topology support. Use the scoped source counterexamples to select evidence, not automatically reject new hypotheses.
avoid_when: A documented standalone/public helper contract can be violated even if internal callers do not exercise that input. Absence of a shipped caller does not disprove an API defect. Strong references prevent identity reuse only for their actual lifetime; they do not prevent mutation, stale metadata, concurrency bugs, or defects after a new caller changes ownership. Seeing a cleanup handler does not prove it is reached exactly once in every cancellation/concurrency path. Existing tests cover only their actual scenarios; a passing suite alone cannot disprove all leak claims. Earlier spread preservation applies only to enumerable own properties actually present at that point; explicit later undefined values, overwrites and changed producers can still lose data. The cited revisions are scoped source/interface counterexamples, not accelerator or general false-positive-rate measurements.

evidence.note: Coalesced request authority and acknowledgement ownership are independent here. Rejecting a second session's hooks does not revoke its admitted request. Native leaf-class controls cover revocation and one-shot acknowledgement, not actual service restarts or all caller timelines.

existingSessionSourcePaths uses archives ?? collectArchivedSources(target, env). The initial missing-index calculation passes a snapshot at line 469, while the recovery recheck omits it at line 477 to reacquire the archive index. The argument difference is not evidence of forgotten archives: unchanged archive-only and missing-source cases agree, while a newly appearing archive invalidates the earlier missing-index view. This supports inspecting optional-argument semantics before making calls identical, not a full migration or concurrency qualification.

handle_async_request catches BaseException and calls _response_closed under AsyncShieldCancellation. The response-body iterator also closes on an exception at lines 579-585. Reading only _receive_stream_event's StreamReset raise omits those owning cleanup paths.

The native RST_STREAM regression follows the rejected first request with a successful second request on the same connection. A first-100-line test excerpt omits it. This public source supplies a relevant control, not a universal semaphore/cancellation proof.

The documented torchrun entry initializes global rank before join/update_weights call check_sglang_ready. A first-120-line excerpt misses that initialization; importing and invoking the helper alone is not this shipped execution path. Static counterexample only, not distributed execution evidence.
QuantizationConfig declares get_supported_act_dtypes as an abstract instance method, independently of the receiver's spelling in an implementation.
The production loader calls the method on quant_config. A class-only TypeError is not a reproduction of this caller's contract.

forward_extend checks the cached object's identity and retains forward_batch in the outer metadata tuple while resolving the next helper result. An isolated id-reuse test omitting that reference does not establish the alleged production failure. This is a revision-bound source observation, not NPU execution evidence.

sameRuntimeIdentity also requires nonzero current.dev/current.ino on Windows. Its self-comparison at activation lines 411-416 can therefore fail and reports identity unavailable; assertPrevious then separately checks the retained object after rename. This counters the constant-dead-code hypothesis, not every possible filesystem race or a runtime-platform qualification.

runPluginDoctorStateMigrationPlans spreads migrated before optionally adding combined notices. With empty collected.notices, migrated.notices remains present; inspecting only the conditional block manufactures a field-loss hypothesis. This is ordered result-expression evidence, not a full Doctor/migration test.

The outer catch converts plugin/runtime JSON.parse errors into candidate failure facts, reports the failed step and returns status=error. A window ending at line 481 omits this handler. Static counterexample to an uncaught-error claim, not native execution or proof that every diagnostic is ideal.
MNNVLCuteDSLConfig.resolve matches static shapes then validates capacity. A new shape-only supports method does not replace those checks or prove hardware support.
The request allows a support-query OR documented fallback and also requires validated new profiles. It does not mandate an invented method or establish backend correctness.
